# Embedding tau

<!-- Generated by scripts/api_docs.py from the code and docs/api/groups.toml. Do not edit. -->

A program that runs sessions itself: the driver and its clock.

Names: `Clock`, `Driver`, `DriverState`, `SystemClock`, `__version__`

## Clock

```python
class Clock(Protocol)
```

What the driver reads time through, so a test can move time itself. `SystemClock` is the
real one.

### Clock.now

```python
def now(self) -> int
```

The current time in milliseconds. It stamps the nodes the driver writes.

## Driver

```python
class Driver
```

Runs one session's cursors over providers, tools, and extensions.

`providers` maps each provider name to the provider a model with that `provider` is
sampled by; each must be named by its own `name`. The program that built them closes
them. `catalog` is where a `Config` node's model name is resolved, at each sample.
`user_config` (`LoadedConfig.user`) is what lets an extension save its options to the user's
file (`Cursor.save_options`, `/config --save`); without it they raise `ConfigError`.

A frontend never calls the driver: it holds a `Client` (`client(id)` makes one, naming
itself), whose calls run on the loop thread, publish what they changed, and poke the pump.
Once the driver has failed or stopped they raise `ConnectionError` (the failure's
`"Type: msg"`, chained, or "the driver is stopped"), as `rest` does; a stream connected then
ends at once. The extensions' commands (`/model` of the
built-in extension `tau` first) run for clients; a command that takes a `Cursor` runs ahead
of the `pre_step` hooks of a step the driver asks for. Aborting or going elsewhere cancels
it. Extensions are listed in the constructor in load order, and checked there like tools
(`DefinitionError`); each hook point runs them by their hook order, then that order (D28:
`ConfigError` for a bad `extensions.NAME.order` in `catalog`). `reload` swaps them for others
while nothing is in flight.

### Driver.__init__

```python
def __init__(
    self,
    session: Session,
    providers: Mapping[str, Provider],
    catalog: ModelCatalog,
    *,
    tools: Sequence[Tool | Callable[..., object]] = (),
    extensions: Sequence[Extension] = (),
    clock: Clock | None = None,
    user_config: UserConfig | None = None,
) -> None
```

### Driver.use_catalog

```python
def use_catalog(self, catalog: ModelCatalog) -> None
```

Resolve model names in `catalog`, and order hooks by it, from the next job
dispatched on (clients get `Commands` if `models()` changed, D32 section 8). `ConfigError`
(nothing changes) for a bad `extensions.NAME.order`.

### Driver.reload

```python
async def reload(self, extensions: Sequence[Extension]) -> None
```

Run `extensions` (listed in load order, as at construction) instead of the ones the
driver has, with the same `tools` (D32 section 4: stop first). Refused, with nothing
changed: `Busy` unless every cursor is at rest with no effect out (it does not wait; retry)
or while another reload runs; `DefinitionError` (or `ConfigError`) if the new set does not
fit, checked before anything stops. Then, while the driver takes no job: the extensions
that leave are stopped in reverse load order (their spawned tasks cancelled, then `stop`;
a failure is reported, not raised), the new set is adopted (options, tools, tool owners,
commands; every folded `Config` forgotten), and the new extensions are started in load
order. An extension object in both lists is neither stopped nor started. Clients are sent
`Commands` if the forms changed. A `start` that fails stops those this reload started, and
the driver adopts the extensions both lists share alone; `ExtensionLoadError` names it.
There is no way back to the old instances: restarting is the safer path. The tree is not
rewritten: a `Config` node that sets options of an extension no longer here (or no longer
fitting its type) fails when it is read (`ConfigError`), not now.

### Driver.start

```python
async def start(self) -> None
```

Run each extension's `start`, in load order, then start the pump. Call inside the
running loop, once. A `start` that raises or outlives its timeout stops the ones started
before it (reverse order) and raises `ExtensionLoadError` naming it; the pump never runs,
and the driver is stopped.

### Driver.stop

```python
async def stop(self) -> None
```

Cancel everything without answering, as a crash would; then stop every started
extension in reverse load order (its spawned tasks cancelled, then its `stop`; a failure is
written to stderr and the next one runs). `rest` and every frontend call raise from now
on; client streams end, later ones at once.

### Driver.state

```python
def state(self) -> DriverState
```

A snapshot of the driver, for a harness.

### Driver.rest

```python
async def rest(self, cursor: int, waiter: int | None = None) -> None
```

Wait until the cursor is at rest with no effect out. Raises `ConnectionError` once the
driver has failed or stopped (also if it does meanwhile). A cursor held by an open
question or a gate does not rest. Returns early if `waiter`, the cursor that waits (a
handle's), is aborted or left meanwhile.

### Driver.client

```python
def client(self, id: str, *, buffer: int = 256) -> LocalClient
```

A client named `id` (stable across reconnects: `john@laptop:tui`), connected now, its
stream opening with the snapshot: make it inside the running loop. `buffer` bounds the
stream (`Feed`).

### Driver.add_item

```python
def add_item(self, to: int, data: ItemData) -> int
```

Add an item to a cursor's scratchpad; the cursor wakes. For whoever has something
to tell a resting cursor from outside a hook: a timer extension, `tau serve` relaying a
webhook. An `ItemData.Input` is what a client's `input` and `send` add (they say who
typed it), so it is refused here. A hook adds its extension's item with its handle's
`add_item`.

## DriverState

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DriverState
    units: int
    queued: bool
    open_questions: int
    parked: int
    failure: Exception | None
    stopped: bool
```

What a harness reads to tell quiet from busy: the effects running (`units`), whether the
pump has something to do (`queued`: a report or poke to take, or a busy cursor with no
effect out; never once the driver has failed or stopped, when the session may be closed),
the questions open, the effects parked in the driver (`parked`: an effect with a question
open or a handle's `rest` or `close_cursor` out waits for an answer or another cursor, and
counts once however many it has out), what the driver died of, and whether it was stopped.
`check` raises `ConnectionError` for a failed or stopped driver, as every client call does
first.

### DriverState.check

```python
def check(self) -> None
```

Raise `ConnectionError` if the driver has failed or is stopped.

## SystemClock

```python
class SystemClock
```

The `Clock` that reads the wall clock. Pass it to `Driver`, which reads time only through
a clock; a test passes its own.

### SystemClock.now

```python
def now(self) -> int
```

The wall-clock time in milliseconds since the epoch.
